title: Adaptive Priority Queuing & Soft-fallback SLO Framework for High-throughput Endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a repeatable framework to define per-endpoint/model SLIs, compute error budgets, and drive automated, priority-aware degradation policies that keep critical customers served during capacity or regional incidents. This ticket defines SLI measurement windows, priority queuing and preemptive shedding, multi-stage circuit breakers, and a soft-fallback model variant strategy (reduced-cost/quantized models) to trade quality for availability gracefully. The goal is to standardize how endpoints declare SLIs, how teams consume error budget, and how the platform enforces adaptive throttling and failover with minimal manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Documented SLI definitions for three endpoint classes (interactive chat, streaming completion, embedding) with measurement windows and percentiles
Error-budget burn-rate rules and a clear enforcement matrix (soft-fallback -> priority-shed -> circuit-breaker -> regional-failover)
Configurable priority queue implementation sketch and API for tenant/route priority tags
Operational runbook for when automatic enforcement triggers (alerts, escalation, rollback path)
Simulation results from the chaos/load test harness showing expected degradation profiles for P0/P1/P2 traffic
Prototype PR that implements priority tagging and a server-side admission gate (feature-flagged behind runtime-1.19)
Dashboard prototype showing per-endpoint SLI, error budget remaining, and current enforcement state
proposed_sli_definitions: Interactive chat endpoint: availability SLI = fraction of requests with latency <= 250ms P50 and <= 600ms P95 measured over 5m windows; correctness SLI for rollout evaluation = regression-free generative quality using daily eval set (binary pass/fail)
Streaming completion endpoint: stream-start SLI = P90 of time-to-first-token < 150ms measured over 1m windows; continuity SLI = fraction of sessions with no stream interruption > 500ms

Embedding endpoint: throughput SLI = 99th percentile request completion latency < 120ms measured over 15m windows; error SLI = fraction of requests returning 20x or fewer tokens than expected (indicates model fault)
All SLIs must be emitted as quantile and count metrics and tagged by region, model_variant, customer_tier, and route
error_budget_policy: Default SLO: 99.5% availability/latency SLI per endpoint per rolling 30d window unless overridden by product
Error budget accounting tiering: allocate budgets by customer_tier (Enterprise, Standard, Free) with Enterprise getting 2x the baseline headroom
Burn-rate policy: automated mitigation triggers when 1h projected burn-rate > 5x (soft mitigation) and > 10x (hard mitigation)
Grace period hooks: short noisy-window allowance (3 x 1m windows) before enforcement to avoid flapping on transient spikes
Manual override path: SRE or on-call can pause automatic shedding for up to 2 hours with annotated justification recorded in incident log
circuit_breaker_rules: Three-stage circuit breaker per route/model_variant: (1) Warning state (log+telemetry), (2) Probation state (reduce concurrency + prioritize tokens), (3) Open state (reject non-priority requests)
State transitions are based on burn-rate, error-rate, and sustained latency thresholds evaluated over 1m/5m/30m windows
Hysteresis configuration: minimum open duration 2m plus geometric backoff for re-try probes; re-close requires sustained healthy metrics for 4x the open duration
Safe-fallback: in Open state attempt best-effort soft-fallback to compatible quantized variant with reduced context-length and quality degradation before rejecting
Expose circuit state as metric and tag for routing decisions and cascade prevention
multi_region_failover: Primary routing preference remains local region for latency; failover policy prefers warm standby region with compatible model_variant and similar quantization profile
Failover triggers: region-level capacity exhaustion OR region health heartbeat drop OR cross-region latency degradation beyond 2x baseline

Failover sequence: (1) route new requests to standby region for P0 customers, (2) apply per-tenant priority queuing in standby region, (3) for remaining traffic enable soft-fallback model variants and preemptively shed P2/P3 traffic
Data residency: do not failover traffic that is marked 'regional-only' by customer policy; provide clear telemetry showing excluded tenants
Warm-standby sync: maintain model cache descriptor parity and quantization metadata within 15 minutes; KV cache warming policy documented
priority_queuing_and_preemptive_shedding: Introduce tenant/request priority token that flows through request metadata; default priority derived from customer_tier + route_tag
Admission policy: admit requests by descending priority until target CPU/GPU headroom threshold reached, calculated per-backend-pool
Preemptive shedding algorithm: compute per-tenant consumption of error budget; if projected to exhaust within next 1h, lower admission priority or cap concurrency for that tenant
Soft-fallback routing: for admitted but resource-constrained requests, prefer variant with reduced compute (e.g., int8 quantized model) and attach quality downgrade header to response
Fairness guardrails: ensure no single tenant can be starved for > 3 minutes unless explicitly exceeding committed capacity
observability_requirements: Emit SLI metrics with tags: endpoint, route, model_variant, tenant, region, priority
Create derived dashboards: per-endpoint error budget remaining, projected burn-rate, current enforcement state, and per-tenant deviation
Tracing: attach decision trace for every rejected/shed request showing reason (circuit-state, priority, error-budget) and relevant metric snapshots
Alerting: burn-rate > 5x for critical endpoints triggers P1 page to SRE; automated mitigation must be documented in alert playbook
Retention: 90d for SLI/SLM metrics, 365d for discrete enforcement events (for post-incident analysis)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Docs + API): finalize schema for SLO declarations and priority tags, publish library for teams to declare endpoint SLIs
Phase 1 (Telemetry): instrument three pilot endpoints (chat, streaming, embedding) and surface dashboards
Phase 2 (Control Plane): implement feature-flagged priority queue and admission gate for a small subset of tenants
Phase 3 (Automation): enable automated soft-fallback and probation circuit-breaker for pilot endpoints in canary region
Phase 4 (Scale): expand to all routes with migration window and provide tooling for product teams to tune per-endpoint parameters
Rollback plan: global feature flag with immediate disable; telemetry-only mode to test side effects before switching enforcement on
test_plan: Unit tests for priority queue scoring and admission gate logic
Integration tests simulating mixed-priority traffic with synthetic tenants and verifying fairness and headroom guarantees
Chaos tests that blackhole a region and verify failover ordering and exclusion rules for region-locked tenants
Load-test scenarios for burn-rates (2x, 5x, 10x) and measurement of quality degradation when soft-fallback is engaged
Runbook drills with SRE to exercise manual override and incident notes capture
